answers.explanation: With nothing cached, the root is the only place to start.
The root only knows who runs each TLD.
The resolver follows the alias by changing SNAME to the canonical name and starting over.
Its cache has .com and example.com delegations, but nothing for .net, so the closest known ancestor of cdn.example.net is the root.
The example.com delegation is cached, so it goes straight to example.com's servers.
Every step is cached, each for its own TTL.
It's dropped from SLIST, and the resolver tries the next server.
The stub made one recursive query and gets one reply back (which includes the CNAME and the A record together).
